rationale: The MIN-of-two-confirmations design is internally consistent and the sign follows naturally from the expression, but it is a fairly incremental hybrid of the archived "Recognized-Intangible Cash Insolvency" and "Pre-R&D Earnings Distress Separator" with R&D intensity swapped in for intangible intensity.

This is a near-mechanical restatement of the archived "Pre-R&D Earnings Distress Separator" (income replaced by book equity plus an R&D stock), and it suffers from internal collinearity because ceq drives both terms in opposite directions, so the product's variation is confounded rather than a clean conditional test.

It reuses the archived "Leveraged Knowledge Sales Validation" template with goodwill substituted for R&D stock, and its expected negative sign for sales contraction runs against both the well-documented growth/investment anomaly (low growth earns higher returns) and the archive's own negative fmb_tstat on the growth-positive version.

The economics of netting R&D out of gross profit before liability scaling are coherent and the sign matches the expression, though it is the fifth instance of the archive's MUL(IND_RANK(xrd/sale), IND_ZSCORE(coverage)) template and partly repackages the known gross-profitability effect.

The rank difference between lt/at and lt/sale is dominated by sales-to-assets, so the signal is largely a rediscovery of the asset-turnover/efficiency effect rather than the claimed "accounting leverage inflation" mechanism, making the stated hypothesis a misattribution of what the expression computes.

This is a substantively motivated nonlinear diagnostic of the archived Soft-Collateral Maturity Gap (whose strong alpha coexisted with a null fmb slope) rather than a cosmetic variant, but the positive-part transform creates a large tie mass at zero that will make the long leg arbitrarily composed and should be checked.
